extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans of MTV/film-and-television awards, and researchers looking for an overview of the MTV Movie & TV Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Encyclopedic overview of the MTV Movie & TV Awards covering history, production, nomination/voting process, award categories (current and retired), special awards, and film-spoof practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded for
rubrics_metrics.description: Film and television.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MTV Movie & TV Awards are presented for achievements in film and television; the awards began as the MTV Movie Awards (film-focused) and adopted the current name when TV categories were added in 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and voting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees are decided by producers and executives at MTV; winners are decided by the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presently voting is done only through an official MTV Movie & TV Awards voting website. Since 2007, polls for several awards have also been voted on through MTV's web and social media presences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production process / broadcast format
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceremony recording/broadcast may be recorded, live, or live-to-tape and production choices affect presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically recorded out of order (hosts first, musical performances, then awards) with edits; post-2006 began to be broadcast live most years; since 2017 often recorded live-to-tape with a one- or two-day delay. Use of seat fillers when nominees depart early is noted. Ceremony format has sometimes split into separate nights (e.g., scripted vs. unscripted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Movie
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Movie (1992–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core 'Best Movie' award presented since the first ceremony in 1992.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Performance in a Movie
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for performance in a movie (2017–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced (or restructured) when movie and television awards were combined in 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Musical Moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Movie & Television award for Best Musical Moment (2017–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category added with the expansion to include television categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Breakthrough Performance / Next Generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognizing a breakthrough performance (known as 'Next Generation' in 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category name has varied; recognizes rising/new performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Comedic Performance (current)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category honoring the best comedic performance (listed among current awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically existed in earlier runs; the category has appeared in various forms over the years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Frightened Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing a performance judged as the most frightened (listed among current awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has appeared as both a current and previously-retired category in different years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Hero
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing a character/performance as the Best Hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has appeared in current and historical award lists with intermittent years (e.g., 2006, 2010–2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Villain
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing the Best Villain (1992–2016 historically and as a current concept).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known as 'Best On-Screen Dirt Bag' in 2012; category has run in multiple forms and years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Kiss
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Kiss (appears among current and retired awards lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-standing fan-popular category; appears in multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fight
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Fight (appears among current and retired awards lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded for on-screen fight sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Duo / Best On-Screen Team / Best Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Duo (known as 'Best On-Screen Team' in 2018 and 'Best Team' in 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes on-screen pairings or ensembles; name has varied by year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Show
rubrics_metrics.description: Television category for Best Show (2017–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced when the awards expanded to explicitly include television categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Performance in a Show
rubrics_metrics.description: Television category recognizing an individual performance in a show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels the movie performance category after expansion to include TV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Host
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Host (appeared in 2017, 2019–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes hosts of shows or specials; included in TV awards timeline intermittently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Competition Series / Best Reality Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Competition Series (2017, 2021–present), known as 'Best Reality Competition' in 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges reality/competition-format series; name/years have varied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Docu-Reality Series / Best Reality Series/Franchise / Best Reality Royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for docu-reality formatted shows (2018–present), previously known by other reality-series names in 2018 and 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name has shifted between 'Best Reality Series/Franchise' and 'Best Reality Royalty' depending on year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Music Documentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for Best Music Documentary (2018, 2021–present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermittent years of presentation; recognizes documentary films about music or musicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired awards — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous categories have been retired or run only in specific years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists many retired awards (below) with years and occasional alternate names; these indicate the show's changing evaluative categories over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Male Performance (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Movie award 'Best Male Performance' (1992–2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the gendered performance awards retired as categories were restructured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Female Performance (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Movie award 'Best Female Performance' (1992–2016 historically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Best Male Performance note about restructuring/retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Song from a Movie (retired / renamings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for songs from movies (1992–2002, 2005, 2009, 2012, 2013–2015) with several alternate names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known as 'Best Musical Sequence' (2000–2002, 2005), 'Best Music' (2012), and 'Best Musical Moment' (2013–2015) in various years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Breakthrough Performance (retired runs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakthrough Performance existed in earlier runs (1992–1998, 2006–2008, 2010–2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category has been retired and reintroduced in different years; later reappeared under similar names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Male Breakthrough Performance (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Male Breakthrough performance award (1999–2005, 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gendered breakout award run in specific years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Female Breakthrough Performance (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Female Breakthrough performance award (historical run).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See male counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Filmmaker (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for new filmmakers (1992–2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also known as the MTVU Student Filmmaker Award in 2007 for the campus-focused run in some years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Desirable Male / Most Desirable Female (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early-era awards recognizing desirability (Most Desirable Male 1992–1996 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects earlier, more pop-culture/teen-focused categories now retired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Action Sequence (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for action sequences (1992–2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized stunts/sequences rather than overall films.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance Sequence (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for dance sequences (1995, 1998, 2001, 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermittent presentation years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Comedic Performance (retired run 1992–2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedic performance category previously ran in earlier decades and has shifted over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category structure and years have varied; page lists both historic runs and current appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Frightened Performance (retired run 2005–2016)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category run historically for performances showing fear (2005–2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also appears among more recent/current categories in later restructurings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best On-Screen Duo (retired runs)
rubrics_metrics.description: On-screen duo/ensemble award (various years 1992–2006, 2013–2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later rebranded in some years as Best Duo / Best On-Screen Team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and pop categories (retired) — examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Various ephemeral or novelty categories have existed, e.g., Best Sandwich in a Movie (1996), Best Shirtless Performance (2013–2015), Sexiest Performance (2006), Dirtiest Mouth Moment (2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories reflect MTV's playful/pop-culture approach and have been retired as the show evolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Cameo (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for notable cameo appearances (2001–2004, 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermittent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Virtual Performance (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing virtual performances (2003, 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare and intermittent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Video Game Based on a Movie (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recognizing video-game tie-ins (2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-off category in some years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Filmmaker on Campus / MTVU Student Filmmaker Award (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campus/student filmmaking award (2006–2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at student filmmakers in the MTVU context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoof / parody-based categories (retired examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories and segments built around spoofs, e.g., Spoof Award, Best Summer Movie You Haven't Seen Yet, Best Summer Movie So Far.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects tradition of film parodies presented during ceremonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best WTF Moment (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for jaw-dropping/gut-wrenching moments (2009–2015; known as 'Best Jaw-Dropping Moment' in 2011 and 'Best Gut-Wrenching Performance' in 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renamings reflect emphasis shifts in different years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Latino Actor (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category ran 2011–2013 to honor Latino actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific demographic-focused category for a brief run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Line from a Movie (retired / intermittent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for memorable lines (2001–2002, 2011), known as 'Best Line' in early years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermittent return years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Cast (retired/intermittent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for ensemble casts (2012, 2016), also known as 'Ensemble Cast' in 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes ensemble achievements rather than individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best On-Screen Transformation (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing notable actor transformations (2013–2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-run category focused on physical/character transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorite Character (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience-choice style award for Favorite Character (2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-run, fan-focused award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer's Biggest Teen Bad-Ass (retired)
rubrics_metrics.description: One-off/short-run pop-culture award (2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects era-specific teen/pop emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Documentary / True Story / Best Action Performance (retired/intermittent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various genre/format-specific awards have appeared and been retired or presented intermittently (e.g., Best Documentary 2016–2017, Best Action Performance 2016, True Story category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category availability has shifted with programming priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movie & Television ephemeral categories (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: One-off or short-run awards such as Most Meme-able Moment (2017, 2019), Best Fight Against the System (2017), Best American Story, Tearjerker, Scene Stealer, Best Real-Life Hero, Here For The Hookup (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect trend-responsive categories added for particular years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired television categories (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Television awards that have been presented and later retired or run intermittently: Best Talk/Topical Show (2021–2022), Best New Unscripted Series, Best Lifestyle Show, Best Real-Life Mystery or Crime Series (2021), Best Comedy/Game Show, Best Dating Show, Best International Reality Series, Best Reality Cast, Best Reality Fight (2021–2022), Best Reality Romance (2022), Best Reality Return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MTV's TV award slate has been adjusted over time; many reality/unscripted-focused categories have had brief runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous awards (Global Superstar, Breakthrough Social Star)
rubrics_metrics.description: One-off or short-run awards such as Global Superstar (2010) and Breakthrough Social Star (2021–2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect social-media and global-star recognition trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifetime Achievement Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Special award given for lifetime contributions (recipient list provided, e.g., Jason Voorhees 1992, The Three Stooges 1993, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a special honor distinct from competitive categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Bucket of Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Special award presented to films (examples: The Breakfast Club 2005; Do the Right Thing 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honors classic or culturally significant films in select years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Special award recognizing long-standing cultural or career impact (recipients listed by year, e.g., Tom Cruise 2005, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given to individuals or franchises as a lifetime/pop-culture recognition distinct from competitive categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trailblazer Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Special award recognizing emerging influential performers (recipients and ages listed for selected years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often highlights young or breakthrough talent (age of recipient noted on page for some years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic Genius Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Special award given to notable comedic performers (recipients include Will Ferrell 2013, Kevin Hart 2015, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-competitive honor recognizing comedic career achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goat Award (special/novelty recognitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of playful/novel recognitions in 2020 (e.g., 'Dance Your A** Off', 'Comedy Giant', 'Dynamic Duo', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often humorous or tongue-in-cheek recognitions tied to a particular ceremony's theme or special presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film parodies / spoofs practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1993, scenes are spoofed—usually from that year's most popular films (and occasionally TV or older movies)—as part of the ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parody segments may include sound/video montages, replacing some original cast with other actors (often hosts), and vary in length from one dialogue gag to several long scenes including action/fight sequences. The page lists yearly examples and notable performers in these spoofs.
